messages:
support_aly: Heads-up: major customer (AcmeHealth) on Dedicated eu-central reporting consistent 429s and "placement failed" for new allocations. P95 latency jumped from 180ms -> 2.1s. Escalating to infra/SRE.

oncall-bot: Alert: dedicated-pool-eu-central GPU utilization 98% over last 10m. Placement failures: 37. Autoscaler cooldowns: 12.

sre_tom: Looking now. Which dedicated pool and tenant id? Any repro steps we can run quickly?

support_aly: Tenant: acme-prod. Pool: ded-eu-central-4g. Repro (customer supplied):

```bash
# single-threaded repro curl
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b-dedicated","input":"<~512 tokens>"}'
```

They run ~25-35 req/s and see immediate 429 or backend error: "placement failed". Also intermittent 503s with long tail.

eng_runtime_meera: Autoscaler logs show repeated scale_up attempts rejected with "insufficient region capacity". Provider reports zero available GPUs in eu-central for the requested instance types.

infra_bot: Recent provider message snippet: "No compatible GPUs available in eu-central-1a/b/c. Allocation requests queued. Estimated retry window unknown. Ticket #SR-9987 submitted."

account_sam: Customer asserts they have reserved capacity entitlements. Can someone confirm operator-visible committed seats for acme-prod? We need to validate entitlement before proposing failover.

billing_jun: Checked. Contract shows committed 4x A100-equivalent reserved for acme-prod (dedicated). Billing shows active reservation but provider-side allocation for those reservations looks to be impaired (no host returned). No invoice anomalies.

sre_tom: Could be noisy-neighbor or single host OOMs blocking placements. I'm seeing one host (host-12f3) with >95% GPU mem pinned by a long-running job from another tenant; eviction attempts failed due to pinned KV cache.

eng_runtime_meera: If we can't place the full model, we can route to a smaller quantized variant as an automated fallback to keep request success but with different perf. Need to coordinate with account for opt-in.

sre_tom: Quick mitigation options (short list):
- throttle new allocations for non-critical tenants in eu-central
- reduce per-worker max_concurrency to lower memory pressure
- enable regional failover for acme-prod to eu-west (if allowed)
- activate model-fallback to quantized-7b-reduced

support_aly: Acme is nervous about cross-region data residency. Their SLA mentions DR but asks us to keep them in the loop. @account_sam can you confirm permitted failover in writing?

account_sam: They have DR clause with cross-region failover allowed for outages; will confirm in 10m. Meanwhile I'm on a call with the customer.

infra_bot: Provider ticket updated: "Capacity shortage affects all A100-family SKUs in eu-central zone. Allocation retries every 5m. No ETA." (ref: SR-9987)

sre_tom: Patch we can apply now to reduce OOM/placement pressure: set pool config to lower concurrency and limit per-worker tokens. Patching ded-eu-central-4g to:

```yaml
# patch snippet
pool: ded-eu-central-4g
max_concurrency_per_worker: 1
max_sequence_length: 1024
eviction_policy: aggressive
```

eng_runtime_meera: I'll roll the patch as a canary to 10% of nodes. Also enabling prefix KV cache eviction for idle sessions.

support_aly: Rolling now, will update customer.

billing_jun: Heads-up: if we failover to eu-west and use on-demand capacity, cost delta will be material. Flagging for sales/finance.

sre_tom: Also seeing increased placement latency for small jobs — indicates global scheduler queue backlog. Throttling new dedicated allocations should give breathing room. I'm initiating a temporary placement-rate limit for non-critical queues.

eng_runtime_meera: Long-term suggestion: implement degraded-mode deployments where a reduced-size model (quantized) is automatically allowed when full model can't be placed instead of failing the request. We'll scope a small rollout this quarter.

oncall-bot: Follow-ups assigned: infra -> escalate provider quota & request cross-region capacity (2h), runtime -> implement canary pool config patch + model-fallback plan (3h), support -> customer comms + confirm failover consent (30m).

sre_tom: For reproducibility, capturing the sequence we used:
1) Run 30 RPS with payload ~512 tokens -> observe 429/placement failed within 30s
2) Check autoscaler logs: see rejected scale_up due to provider no-capacity
3) Check host metrics: host-12f3 pinned GPU mem >90%
4) Attempt eviction -> failed (pinned cache)

support_aly: Customer confirms errors started around 10:43 UTC and spikes aligned with their traffic surge. They accepted temporary cross-region failover as contingency if we sign off.

account_sam: Confirmed in writing, acme-prod grants permission to failover for incident mitigation. Documented.

infra_bot: Provider updated SR-9987: requested reallocation and priority for reserved tenants. No firm ETA. Also asked for alternative instance family suggestions.

sre_tom: Actioning a conservative failover for acme-prod to eu-west with sticky routing so sessions can complete. Will monitor latency/regression.

eng_runtime_meera: Also enabling model-fallback for acme-prod: requests will prefer redwood-7b-dedicated, fallback to redwood-7b-quantized if placement fails. This preserves success rate at cost of lower quality.

billing_jun: Noted. Sending internal cost-impact alert to sales and finance.

support_aly: Customer says they can tolerate slightly lower quality for now. Appreciate the quick response.

sre_tom: I'll post detailed logs and the full repro capture to the incident ticket after I finish collecting, and keep this thread updated.

oncall-bot: Incident status -> mitigation: in progress. Next update in 30m.
